body.statement: For every fixed \(r\) and every \(c\in(\underline c,\overline c)\), there exist dimensions \(N,T\to\infty\) and deterministic arrays \(d,qvec,a,b,\Lambda,F\) such that \(c_N\to c\), \(\eta_{NT}\to\eta\in\operatorname{int}(\mathcal E_{\mathrm{loc}})\), \(\Lambda^{\top}d=\Lambda^{\top}a_S=0\), \(F^{\top}qvec=F^{\top}b_S=0\), the full Gram limits \(N^{-1}\Lambda^{\top}\Lambda\) and \(T^{-1}F^{\top}F\) are positive definite, the selector-restricted limits \(N^{-1}\Lambda^{\top}M_d\Lambda\) and \(T^{-1}F^{\top}M_{qvec}F\) are positive definite, and the loading, factor, and treatment-score rows are uniformly bounded. Hence the exact-oracle triangular-array class is nonempty without imposing any rule for selecting a minimizer of \(\Phi_{\eta,h}\).
body.justification: The sensitivity experiment must contain concrete deterministic sequences rather than rely on mutually inconsistent oracle restrictions.
body.gap: This is a nonvacuity certificate for the paper's abstract class, not a claim that the restrictions are observable or operationally constructible.
body.consumer: It validates that the absorption phase law is evaluated on a nonempty confounding-free oracle class.
body.proof_tex:
First, the restriction on \(c\) in the proposed statement is necessary.  By the definitions of \(\eta\) and \(\mathcal E_{\mathrm{loc}}\), the first coordinate of \(\eta\) is \(c\), whereas the first-coordinate projection of \(\operatorname{int}(\mathcal E_{\mathrm{loc}})\) is \((\underline c,\overline c)\).  Thus the frozen statement cannot hold when \(c=\underline c\) or \(c=\overline c\).

We now prove the corrected statement constructively.  Fix \(c\in(\underline c,\overline c)\) and a fixed \(r\).  Put
\[
 \mu^\circ=\frac{\underline\mu+\overline\mu}{2},
 \qquad
 v^\circ=\frac{\underline v+\overline v}{2}.
\]
The assumed strict inequalities \(0<\underline\mu<\overline\mu\) and \(0<\underline v<\overline v\) imply
\[
 \mu^\circ\in(\underline\mu,\overline\mu),
 \qquad
 v^\circ\in(\underline v,\overline v).
\]
For every sufficiently large integer \(k\), let
\[
 s_k=\lfloor ck\rfloor,\qquad T_k=4k,\qquad N_k=4s_k.
\]
Then \(N_k,T_k\to\infty\), and the definition \(c_N=N/T\) gives
\[
 c_{N_k}=\frac{N_k}{T_k}
 =\frac{s_k}{k}\longrightarrow c.
\]
Because \(c\) is strictly between the two aspect-ratio bounds, \(c_{N_k}\in(\underline c,\overline c)\) for all sufficiently large \(k\).

Suppress the index \(k\) on the arrays.  Define the support indicators by
\[
 d_i=\mathbf 1\{1\le i\le 2s_k\},
 \qquad
 qvec_t=\mathbf 1\{1\le t\le 2k\}.
\]
Consequently \(n_1=d^\top d=2s_k\), \(t_1=qvec^\top qvec=2k\), and hence
\[
 p_N=\frac{n_1}{N_k}=\frac12,
 \qquad
 q_T=\frac{t_1}{T_k}=\frac12.
\]
Define the score arrays by
\[
 a_i=
 \begin{cases}
 \mu^\circ+(-1)^i\sqrt{v^\circ},&1\le i\le 2s_k,\\
 0,&2s_k<i\le4s_k,
 \end{cases}
 \qquad
 b_t=
 \begin{cases}
 \mu^\circ+(-1)^t\sqrt{v^\circ},&1\le t\le 2k,\\
 0,&2k<t\le4k.
 \end{cases}
\]
Since \(a\) and \(b\) vanish off their respective supports, the definitions \(a_S=d\odot a\) and \(b_S=qvec\odot b\) give \(a_S=a\) and \(b_S=b\).  Each supported set has even cardinality, so it contains equally many plus and minus signs.  The definitions of the supported means therefore yield
\[
 \mu_{a,N}
 =\frac{1}{2s_k}\sum_{i=1}^{2s_k}
   \left(\mu^\circ+(-1)^i\sqrt{v^\circ}\right)
 =\mu^\circ,
 \qquad
 \mu_{b,T}
 =\frac{1}{2k}\sum_{t=1}^{2k}
   \left(\mu^\circ+(-1)^t\sqrt{v^\circ}\right)
 =\mu^\circ.
\]
After subtracting these means, every supported squared deviation equals \(v^\circ\).  The definitions of \(v_{a,N}\) and \(v_{b,T}\) thus give
\[
 v_{a,N}
 =\frac{1}{2s_k}\sum_{i=1}^{2s_k}v^\circ
 =v^\circ,
 \qquad
 v_{b,T}
 =\frac{1}{2k}\sum_{t=1}^{2k}v^\circ
 =v^\circ.
\]

Suppose first that \(r\ge1\), and let \(e_1,\ldots,e_r\) denote the standard basis of \(\mathbb R^r\).  Define
\[
 \rho(j)=1+((j-1)\bmod r).
\]
For all sufficiently large \(k\), \(2s_k\ge r\) and \(2k\ge r\).  Define the rows of the loading and factor matrices by
\[
 \Lambda_{i\cdot}=
 \begin{cases}
 0,&1\le i\le2s_k,\\
 e_{\rho(i-2s_k)}^\top,&2s_k<i\le4s_k,
 \end{cases}
 \qquad
 F_{t\cdot}=
 \begin{cases}
 0,&1\le t\le2k,\\
 e_{\rho(t-2k)}^\top,&2k<t\le4k.
 \end{cases}
\]
The nonzero rows of \(\Lambda\) occur only where \(d_i=0\), while \(a_S\) is zero there.  Hence, term by term,
\[
 \Lambda^\top d=\sum_{i=1}^{N_k}\Lambda_{i\cdot}^\top d_i=0,
 \qquad
 \Lambda^\top a_S=\sum_{i=1}^{N_k}\Lambda_{i\cdot}^\top(a_S)_i=0.
\]
Likewise, the nonzero rows of \(F\) occur only where \(qvec_t=0\), while \(b_S\) is zero there, and therefore
\[
 F^\top qvec=0,\qquad F^\top b_S=0.
\]

For \(\ell\in\{1,\ldots,r\}\), let
\[
 n_{\ell,k}=\#\{1\le j\le2s_k:\rho(j)=\ell\},
 \qquad
 f_{\ell,k}=\#\{1\le j\le2k:\rho(j)=\ell\}.
\]
The cyclic allocation implies
\[
 \left|n_{\ell,k}-\frac{2s_k}{r}\right|\le1,
 \qquad
 \left|f_{\ell,k}-\frac{2k}{r}\right|\le1.
\]
Direct multiplication of the displayed row definitions gives
\[
 \frac1{N_k}\Lambda^\top\Lambda
 =\operatorname{diag}\left(
   \frac{n_{1,k}}{4s_k},\ldots,\frac{n_{r,k}}{4s_k}
  \right)
 \longrightarrow \frac1{2r}I_r
\]
and
\[
 \frac1{T_k}F^\top F
 =\operatorname{diag}\left(
   \frac{f_{1,k}}{4k},\ldots,\frac{f_{r,k}}{4k}
  \right)
 \longrightarrow \frac1{2r}I_r.
\]
By the definitions of \(M_d\) and \(M_{qvec}\), the support placement gives \(M_d\Lambda=\Lambda\) and \(M_{qvec}F=F\).  Consequently
\[
 \frac1{N_k}\Lambda^\top M_d\Lambda
 =\frac1{N_k}\Lambda^\top\Lambda
 \longrightarrow\frac1{2r}I_r,
 \qquad
 \frac1{T_k}F^\top M_{qvec}F
 =\frac1{T_k}F^\top F
 \longrightarrow\frac1{2r}I_r.
\]
Both limits are positive definite.  Moreover, for all sufficiently large \(k\), every cyclic count is positive, so both \(\Lambda\) and \(F\) have column rank \(r\), and therefore \(\Lambda F^\top\) has rank \(r\).  If \(r=0\), take \(\Lambda\) and \(F\) to be the unique matrices with zero columns; all four orthogonality equalities hold and the Gram assertions are vacuous under the standard zero-dimensional convention.

Every row of \(\Lambda\) and \(F\) has Euclidean norm at most \(1\).  Also,
\[
 \max_i|a_i|\le\mu^\circ+\sqrt{v^\circ},
 \qquad
 \max_t|b_t|\le\mu^\circ+\sqrt{v^\circ}.
\]
Thus the loading, factor, and treatment-score rows are uniformly bounded in \(k\).

Collecting the calculations above,
\[
 \eta_{N_kT_k}
 =\left(c_{N_k},\frac12,\frac12,
         \mu^\circ,v^\circ,\mu^\circ,v^\circ\right)
 \longrightarrow
 \eta
 =\left(c,\frac12,\frac12,
         \mu^\circ,v^\circ,\mu^\circ,v^\circ\right).
\]
The condition \(\underline\pi\in(0,1/2)\) puts both share coordinates strictly inside \([\underline\pi,1-\underline\pi]\).  The strict inequalities already established for \(c,\mu^\circ,v^\circ\) put every other coordinate in the interior of its corresponding factor of \(\mathcal E_{\mathrm{loc}}\); in particular, each mean lies in the interior of the positive component \([\underline\mu,\overline\mu]\).  Hence \(\eta\in\operatorname{int}(\mathcal E_{\mathrm{loc}})\).

This construction uses only \(c,r\) and the fixed envelope constants.  It does not invoke \(\Phi_{\eta,h}\), \(h\), an argmin of \(\Phi_{\eta,h}\), or any selection from such an argmin.  It therefore supplies the asserted nonempty exact-oracle triangular-array class independently of any minimizer-selection rule.
